赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Tianchen Deng, Zhenxiang Xiong, Nailin Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Jiuming Liu
赵波老师实验室.summary: Mamba-VGGT introduces a Sliding Window Mamba memory module enhancing long-sequence video geometry grounding, mitigating geometric drift while maintaining spatial consistency and reducing errors.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers (VGGT) have set new benchmarks in high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction. However, as the sequence length increases, these models suffer from catastrophic geometric forgetting and accumulation drift, primarily due to the quadratic complexity of global attention which necessitates truncated temporal windows. To overcome the resulting geometric drift, we present Mamba-VGGT, an enhanced VGGT framework capable of persistent long-range reasoning. Our key contribution is a Sliding Window Mamba (SWM) memory module that maintains an explicit external memory token across temporal windows. This module leverages selective state-space modeling to distill and propagate global geometric priors, effectively bypassing the memory constraints of traditional transformers. To integrate these long-term temporal cues without disrupting the highly optimized spatial features of the pre-trained VGGT, we propose a Zero-Init Spatial Memory Injector. Utilizing zero-convolutional layers, this injector adaptively fuses persistent memory into the patch token stream, ensuring structural stability and seamless feature alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing VGGT-based methods in maintaining spatial consistency and reducing trajectory accumulation errors. Our work provides a scalable, linear-complexity solution for geometry-grounded world modeling in extensive 3D environments.

赵波老师实验室.title: Attention Hijacking: Response Manipulation Across Queries in Vision-Language Models
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Zhiqiang Wang, Dongrui Liu, Yan Li, Zonghao Ying, Wei Xue
赵波老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces "Attention Hijacking," an adversarial attack that enhances cross-query response manipulation in vision-language models by stabilizing image-dominant attention patterns.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Existing adversarial attacks on vision-language models (VLMs) can steer model outputs toward attacker-specified target responses, but their effectiveness often degrades when the same perturbed input is paired with different textual queries. This paper studies cross-query response manipulation, where a single adversarial example is expected to remain effective across diverse user queries. We first analyze the limitations of existing attacks and find that successful transfer is closely associated with preserving an image-dominant attention pattern during response generation. Motivated by the observation, we propose \textbf{Attention Hijacking}, a novel adversarial attack that explicitly steers internal attention distributions toward a persistent image-dominant pattern. By amplifying the influence of visual tokens on target response tokens while suppressing the competing influence of textual tokens, our method reduces the dependence of the manipulated output on the specific wording of the query. Extensive experiments on widely used VLMs show that Attention Hijacking substantially improves cross-query transferability across diverse target responses and unseen queries. The method also extends effectively to multiple attack scenarios, offering new insights into the role of attention stability in transferable response manipulation for VLMs.

赵波老师实验室.title: Skills on the Fly: Test-Time Adaptive Skill Synthesis for LLM Agents
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Jingxing Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Zhihui Fu, Jun Wang, Weiwen Liu
赵波老师实验室.summary: The SkillTTA method enhances LLM agents' adaptability by synthesizing task-specific skills from relevant training trajectories, improving performance on various benchmarks without updating the solver model.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: LLM agents benefit from reusable skills, yet test-time tasks often require guidance more specific than a static skill library can provide. We propose \emph{SkillTTA}, a Test-Time Adaptive Skill Synthesis method that retrieves a small set of training trajectories relevant to the current task and synthesizes them into a temporary, task-specific textual skill. The solver model is kept fixed, so adaptation happens entirely through generated context rather than parameter updates. We evaluate the method on SpreadsheetBench, ALFWorld, and BigCodeBench. Compared with static trajectory-to-skill synthesis using GPT-5.5, task-specific skills improve SpreadsheetBench Pass@1 from 0.397 to 0.505 and BigCodeBench Pass@1 from 0.517 to 0.651. On ALFWorld, the method matches a heavier memory-learning baseline within four points of success rate while producing the shortest successful trajectories among reported methods. Ablations on SpreadsheetBench further show that synthesized skills outperform raw trajectory prompting, that top-$k$ retrieval should stay small, and that failed trajectories are especially useful because they expose recurring evaluator-facing mistakes.

赵波老师实验室.title: VGGT-Occ: Geometry-Grounded and Density-Aware Gated Fusion for 3D Occupancy Prediction
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Xun Chen, Tianchen Deng, Rui Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Junyi Ma
赵波老师实验室.summary: VGGT-Occ introduces a geometry-infused framework with Projection-Aware Deformable Attention for enhanced 3D occupancy prediction, achieving superior performance with fewer parameters.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction requires accurate 2D-to-3D feature lifting, yet current methods restrict camera geometry to initial projections. Subsequent operations like offset learning, attention weighting, and cross-camera aggregation remain geometry-agnostic, ignoring essential physical constraints. We propose VGGT-Occ, a framework that embeds geometric tokens throughout the entire pipeline. We introduce Projection-Aware Deformable Attention (PA-DA) to inject geometry into all attention stages. PA-DA projects 3D offsets back to image planes and leverages the projection Jacobian as an additive bias to suppress unreliable observations. Features are then integrated through a view-quality semantic gate for cross-view consistency. To optimize both efficiency and performance, we employ a sequential coarse-to-fine decoder with gated fusion, where low-resolution features are refined into higher resolutions, allocating computation by information density while substantially reducing decoder cost. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our approach. On SurroundOcc-nuScenes, VGGT-Occ achieves 33.00\% IoU and 21.08\% mIoU ($T{=}1$), and 33.64\% IoU and 21.43\% mIoU with $T{=}2$ inference, outperforming existing methods, with only ${\sim}41$M trainable parameters in the occupancy head. Code will be released publicly.

赵波老师实验室.title: OrbiSim: World Models as Differentiable Physics Engines for Embodied Intelligence
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Jiajian Li, Jingyuan Huang, Junru Gong, Qi Wang, Xiaokang Yang
赵波老师实验室.summary: OrbiSim is a differentiable physics engine that unifies structured scene assets and neural dynamics to enhance robotic simulation and reinforcement learning performance.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: We present OrbiSim, a novel robotic simulation paradigm that redefines world models as a fully differentiable physics engine for embodied intelligence. Unlike prior world models that focus on unconstrained imagination in latent or visual domains, OrbiSim establishes a unified, physically-grounded pathway that bridges structured scene assets, neural dynamics, and downstream reinforcement learning. By enabling end-to-end differentiability throughout the entire simulation loop -- spanning from explicit state transitions to visual observation generation -- OrbiSim supports tasks traditionally intractable for classical simulators, such as differentiable contact modeling, gradient-based policy optimization under sparse rewards, and intuitive physical inference. Empirical results demonstrate that OrbiSim significantly outperforms state-of-the-art world models in both predictive fidelity and control performance. Furthermore, its consistent responsiveness to asset configurations and physical parameters suggests its potential as a differentiable tool for enhancing robot simulation and policy training.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Dexora: Open-source VLA for High-DoF Bimanual Dexterity
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zongzheng Zhang, Jingrui Pang, Zhuo Yang, Kun Li, Minwen Liao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Dexora is an open-source Vision-Language-Action model enabling high-dimensional dexterous manipulation with dual-arm systems, surpassing existing benchmarks through innovative training methods and data quality management.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently become a central direction in embodied AI, but current systems are restricted to either dual-gripper control or single-arm dexterous hand manipulation. While low-dimensional gripper control can often be handled with simpler methods, high-dimensional dexterous hand control benefits greatly from full end-to-end VLA learning. In this work, we introduce Dexora, the first open-source VLA system that natively targets dual-arm, dual-hand high-DoF manipulation. We design a hybrid teleoperation pipeline that decouples gross arm kinematics (captured with a custom exoskeleton backpack) from fine finger motion (markerless hand tracking via Apple Vision Pro), and that drives both a physical dual-arm dual-hand platform and an identical MuJoCo digital twin. Using that interface, we assemble a large training corpus: an embodiment-matched synthetic corpus (100K simulated trajectories, 6.5M frames) and a real-world dataset of 10K teleoperated episodes (2.92M frames). To mitigate noisy teleoperation demonstrations, we propose a data-quality-aware training recipe: an offline discriminator provides clip-level weights for diffusion-transformer policy training, down-weighting low-quality demonstrations. Empirically, Dexora outperforms competitive VLA baselines on both basic and dexterous benchmarks (e.g., average dexterous success 66.7% vs. 51.7%), attains 90% success on basic tasks, and shows robust out-of-distribution and cross-embodiment generalization. Ablations confirm the importance of real data and the discriminator for dexterity.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: WorldArena 2.0: Extending Embodied World Model Benchmarking on Modality, Functionality and Platform
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yu Shang, Yinzhou Tang, Yiding Ma, Zhuohang Li, Lei Jin
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: WorldArena 2.0 is a comprehensive benchmark that enhances embodied world model evaluation by incorporating multimodal perception, interactive functionality, and diverse real-world platforms.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: World models have emerged as a central paradigm for embodied intelligence, enabling agents to predict action-conditioned future and reason about environmental dynamics. However, existing embodied world model benchmarks are still largely confined to vision-only prediction, offline embodied applications, and simulator-based evaluation, making them insufficient for assessing increasingly comprehensive world models. In this work, we introduce WorldArena 2.0, an expanded benchmark that systematically broadens embodied world model evaluation along three dimensions: modality, functionality, and platform. Along the modality dimension, WorldArena 2.0 extends evaluation from vision-only to visuotactile modalities, enabling assessment of multimodal perception and prediction. Along the functionality dimension, it extends beyond policy evaluation and planning to assess world models as interactive RL environments for policy optimization. Along the platform dimension, it moves beyond simulator-only evaluation to a diverse suite of simulated and real-world robotic settings across multiple embodiments. Under a standardized protocol, WorldArena 2.0 comprehensively evaluates perceptual quality, interactive utility, and cross-platform performance, providing a comprehensive testbed for tracking progress toward embodied world models. The benchmark is available at: this https URL.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: VoxScene: Anchor-Conditioned Voxel Diffusion for Indoor Scene Arrangement
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Haotian Mao, Yuhan Huang, Jiatao Lin, Yang Zhao, Hui Wang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: VoxScene introduces an anchor-conditioned voxel diffusion framework for 3D scene synthesis, ensuring collision-free arrangements and high-fidelity voxel outputs in complex environments.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: We present VoxScene, a novel anchor-conditioned voxel diffusion framework tailored for 3D scene synthesis. Current data-driven layout generation techniques typically rely on bounding proxies or implicit representations, which overlook volumetric structures. This geometric blindness inevitably leads to severe physical collisions and structural entanglement, particularly in densely populated environments. To overcome these limitations, we shift the paradigm to an explicit, object-centric voxel representation. Our pipeline sequentially synthesizes discrete volumetric occupancies conditioned on prior anchors and local context. By exploiting the mutually exclusive nature of discrete voxels, our approach eliminates spatial ambiguities and guarantees collision-free arrangements, even in highly complex environments. Furthermore, the synthesized high-fidelity voxel grids serve as discriminative geometric queries for downstream asset retrieval. Extensive experiments demonstrate the universality of our method, achieving state-of-the-art physical plausibility and unlocking shape diversity compared to existing layout planners.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Resolving Representation Ambiguity in Feedforward Novel View Synthesis Transformer via Semantic-Spatial Decoupling
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yihang Wu, Yihang Sun, Shaofeng Zhang, Zuxuan Wu, Junchi Yan
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents a novel approach for feedforward novel view synthesis transformers that decouples semantic and spatial representations to enhance rendering fidelity without increasing inference latency.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Transformer-based models have advanced feedforward novel view synthesis (NVS). Current architectures such as GS-LRM and LVSM mix semantic information (e.g., RGB) and spatial information (e.g., Plücker rays) into a shared feature space. Since Plücker rays naturally carry lattice-like spatial structure, these designs can make the spatial bias interfere with appearance representation and degrade rendering fidelity. To this end, we propose to decouple the representation of feedforward NVS transformers into separate semantic and spatial tokens. The decoupled design keeps semantic and spatial information explicit in their branches while preserving cross-branch interaction through shared attention routing. Built on this design, we introduce optional categorized supervision and bidirectional modulation: the former provides branch-specific training signals, while the latter improves interaction between the two branches. Notably, the base decoupled design introduces virtually zero additional inference latency due to its architectural design. The proposed designs achieve consistent improvements, demonstrating effectiveness across decoder-only and encoder-decoder feedforward NVS models.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Bench2Drive-Robust: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving under Deployment Perturbations
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhenghao Jin, Yanlun Peng, Xianda Guo, Haoran Liu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Bench2Drive-Robust introduces a device-centric benchmark for evaluating closed-loop autonomous driving robustness against realistic deployment perturbations, highlighting significant challenges often overlooked by traditional methods.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Robustness is a critical requirement for deploying autonomous driving systems in the real world. Existing robustness benchmarks for autonomous driving have made important progress in studying the effects of image-level corruptions, such as adverse weather or camera degradation, on perception modules and open-loop planning outputs. However, deployment can also involve system-level imperfections, such as inference latency and ego-state estimation errors, which remain less studied in closed-loop E2E-AD evaluation. These imperfections can accumulate through the feedback loop and destabilize control. In this work, we present Bench2Drive-Robust, to our knowledge the first device-centric robustness benchmark for closed-loop end-to-end autonomous driving under realistic deployment perturbations. We systematically evaluate deployment-oriented perturbations arising from three major sources: camera-stream failures (frame drop, partial observation), ego-state estimation errors (GPS noise, and speed or odometry errors), and compute-induced control delay (model inference delay). We evaluate representative end-to-end driving methods and analyze their robustness under different perturbation severities. Our results show that these deployment-related perturbations can substantially degrade closed-loop driving performance, revealing robustness challenges that are not fully captured by conventional image-level corruption evaluations. By establishing a closed-loop evaluation protocol and demonstrating the substantial impact of these deployment-oriented perturbations, Bench2Drive-Robust defines practical robustness problems for end-to-end autonomous driving and encourages further research on deployment-aware robust driving systems.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: An Efficient Streaming Video Understanding Framework with Agentic Control
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Jinming Liu, Jianguo Huang, Zhaoyang Jia, Jiahao Li, Xiaoyi Zhang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The R3-Streaming framework enhances dynamic video understanding by using an adaptive cascaded control approach for efficient memory management and compute routing, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Streaming video requires handling dynamic information density under strict latency budgets. Yet, existing methods typically employ static strategies, such as fixed memory compression or reliance on a single model, forcing a trade-off: fast models fail on complex queries, while always-on heavy models violate real-time constraints and overcomplicate simple queries. Rather than fixing these decisions upfront, we propose R3-Streaming (Remember, Respond, Reason), which formulates streaming video understanding as a cascaded control problem: for each query, the system compresses memory, judges response readiness, and routes computation sequentially, so that each downstream decision builds on progressively refined information states. To optimize this pipeline, we introduce an age-aware forgetting policy for memory compression, as aggressively compressing historical frames can yield substantial performance gains. For compute routing, we propose TB-GRPO, a target-balanced reinforcement learning objective that routes hard queries to a stronger model while preventing mode collapse. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that R3-Streaming achieves state-of-the-art results among streaming MLLMs, reaching 57.92 on OVO-Bench and 76.36 on StreamingBench, while reducing visual token usage by 95 to 96 percent.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Entropy-Gradient Inversion: Moving Toward Internal Mechanism of Large Reasoning Models
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Junyao Yang, Chen Qian, Kun Wang, Linfeng Zhang, Quanshi Zhang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper introduces Entropy-Gradient Inversion and Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO) to enhance reasoning capabilities in Large Reasoning Models through improved reinforcement learning techniques.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: The advancement of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift from reactive ``fast thinking'' text generation to systematic, step-by-step ``slow thinking'' reasoning, unlocking state-of-the-art performance in complex mathematical and logical tasks. However, the field faces \textit{the fundamental gap between token-level behavioral analysis and internal reasoning mechanisms, and the instability of reinforcement learning (RL) for reasoning optimization relying on costly external verifiers}. We identify and formally define \textbf{Entropy-Gradient Inversion}, a robust negative correlation between token entropy and logit gradients that acts as a definitive geometric fingerprint for LRM reasoning capability. Building on this, we propose \textbf{Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO)}, which embeds this inversion signature into RL reward regularization. Extensive experiments on various reasoning benchmarks across multiple model scales show CorR-PO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, confirming that stronger inversion directly correlates with superior reasoning performance.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Dynamic Execution Commitment of Vision-Language-Action Models
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Feng Chen, Xianghui Wang, Yuxuan Chen, Boying Li, Yefei He
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper introduces A3, an Adaptive Action Acceptance mechanism that optimizes dynamic execution commitment in Vision-Language-Action models by improving reliability and efficiency without manual horizon tuning.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models predominantly adopt action chunking, i.e., predicting and committing to a short horizon of consecutive low-level actions in a single forward pass, to amortize the inference cost of large-scale backbones and reduce per-step latency. However, committing these multi-step predictions to real-world execution requires balancing success rate against inference efficiency, a decision typically governed by fixed execution horizons tuned per task. Such heuristics ignore the state-dependent nature of predictive reliability, leading to brittle performance in dynamic or out-of-distribution settings. In this paper, we introduce A3, an Adaptive Action Acceptance mechanism that reframes dynamic execution commitment as a self-speculative prefix verification problem. A3 first computes a trajectory-wise consensus score of actions via group sampling, then selects a representative draft and prioritizes downstream verification. Specifically, it enforces: (1) consensus-ordered conditional invariance, which validates low-consensus actions by judging whether they remain consistent when re-decoded conditioned on high-consensus actions; and (2) prefix-closed sequential consistency, which guarantees physical rollout integrity by accepting only the longest continuous sequence of verified actions starting from the beginning. Consequently, the execution horizon emerges as the longest verifiable prefix satisfying both internal model logic and sequential execution constraints. Experiments across diverse VLA models and benchmarks demonstrate that A3 eliminates the need for manual horizon tuning while achieving a superior trade-off between execution robustness and inference throughput.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: UST-Hand: An Uncertainty-aware Spatiotemporal Point Cloud Interaction Network for 3D Self-supervised Hand Pose Estimation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Tianhao Han, Haoyang Zhang, Liang Xie, Haochen Chang, Kun Gao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: UST-Hand introduces a robust self-supervised 3D hand pose estimation framework that leverages uncertainty modeling and probabilistic point clouds to enhance accuracy and stability against noise.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Manually annotating accurate 3D hand poses is extremely time-consuming and labor-intensive. Existing self-supervised hand pose estimation methods leverage the discrepancy between input images and rendered outputs, or multi-view consistency constraints, as the driving force to optimize networks and progressively refine pose accuracy. However, these methods are highly susceptible to noisy pseudo-labels and overlook the importance of fully exploiting fine-grained spatial correlations, which undermines the stability of model training. To address these issues, we propose UST-Hand, a self-supervised learning framework that estimates uncertainty distribution of hand pose and constructs a probabilistic point cloud feature space, which enables the complex spatiotemporal relationship modeling. UST-Hand employs a conditional normalizing flow model to capture hand pose distributions and samples diverse hypotheses, facilitating robust learning under noisy pseudo-labels supervision with enhanced stability. These multi-hypothesis are mapped to a unified probabilistic 3D point cloud space for multi-view and temporal feature interaction, comprehensively exploring hand motion patterns and fine-grained spatial correlations. Extensive experiments on three challenging datasets demonstrate that UST-Hand achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing self-supervised methods by up to 37.8% in Mean Per Vertex Position Error (MPVPE).

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Rethinking Point Clouds as Sequences: A Causal Next-Token Predictive Learning Framework
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yumeng Yao, Jingzhi Dong, Haowen Gu, Tao Chen, Zonghan Wu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: This paper introduces PointNTP, a novel approach for point cloud pre-training that utilizes a causal transformer for next-token prediction, enhancing self-supervised learning without reconstruction decoders.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: With the rapid progress of multimodal foundation models and predictive pre-training, an important open question is how to equip 3D point clouds with a pre-training paradigm that is better aligned with next-token and next-embedding learning. Existing point-cloud self-supervised methods are largely built on masked reconstruction or explicit geometric generation, and thus remain tied to input recovery rather than predictive dependency modeling. In this paper, we introduce PointNTP, which reformulates point cloud pre-training as a fully causal, decoder-free latent Next-Token Prediction problem. Specifically, each point cloud is first partitioned into local patches and serialized into a structured 3D token sequence according to patch-center geometry. The resulting sequence is then modeled by a causal Transformer under prefix-only conditioning, and trained with a shift-based prediction objective stabilized by stop-gradient targets. This design enables the model to learn structural dependencies directly in latent space, without reconstruction decoders or explicit geometric recovery. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed PointNTP is highly competitive across multiple downstream tasks: it achieves 93.8%(+0.5%), 92.6%(+0.3%), and 89.3%(+1.1%) on OBJ_BG, OBJ_ONLY, and PB_T50_RS of ScanObjectNN, respectively; obtains 85.0%(+0.1%) in this http URL on ShapeNetPart; and reaches 71.1% mAcc on S3DIS Area 5. Overall, decoder-free causal latent prediction provides a simple, scalable, and potentially modality-agnostic paradigm for point-cloud self-supervised learning, offering a new 3D perspective on foundation-style predictive learning for 3D data.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: VGGT-Occ: Geometry-Grounded and Density-Aware Gated Fusion for 3D Occupancy Prediction
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Xun Chen, Tianchen Deng, Rui Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Junyi Ma
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: VGGT-Occ introduces a geometry-infused framework with Projection-Aware Deformable Attention for enhanced 3D occupancy prediction, achieving superior performance with fewer parameters.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: OrbiSim: World Models as Differentiable Physics Engines for Embodied Intelligence
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Jiajian Li, Jingyuan Huang, Junru Gong, Qi Wang, Xiaokang Yang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: OrbiSim is a differentiable physics engine that unifies structured scene assets and neural dynamics to enhance robotic simulation and reinforcement learning performance.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: We present OrbiSim, a novel robotic simulation paradigm that redefines world models as a fully differentiable physics engine for embodied intelligence. Empirical results demonstrate that OrbiSim significantly outperforms state-of-the-art world models in both predictive fidelity and control performance. Furthermore, its consistent responsiveness to asset configurations and physical parameters suggests its potential as a differentiable tool for enhancing robot simulation and policy training.

ReThinkLab.title: Dexora: Open-source VLA for High-DoF Bimanual Dexterity
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zongzheng Zhang, Jingrui Pang, Zhuo Yang, Kun Li, Minwen Liao
ReThinkLab.summary: Dexora is an open-source Vision-Language-Action model enabling high-dimensional dexterous manipulation with dual-arm systems, surpassing existing benchmarks through innovative training methods and data quality management.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently become a central direction in embodied AI, but current systems are restricted to either dual-gripper control or single-arm dexterous hand manipulation. While low-dimensional gripper control can often be handled with simpler methods, high-dimensional dexterous hand control benefits greatly from full end-to-end VLA learning. In this work, we introduce Dexora, the first open-source VLA system that natively targets dual-arm, dual-hand high-DoF manipulation. We design a hybrid teleoperation pipeline that decouples gross arm kinematics (captured with a custom exoskeleton backpack) from fine finger motion (markerless hand tracking via Apple Vision Pro), and that drives both a physical dual-arm dual-hand platform and an identical MuJoCo digital twin. Using that interface, we assemble a large training corpus: an embodiment-matched synthetic corpus (100K simulated trajectories, 6.5M frames) and a real-world dataset of 10K teleoperated episodes (2.92M frames). To mitigate noisy teleoperation demonstrations, we propose a data-quality-aware training recipe: an offline discriminator provides clip-level weights for diffusion-transformer policy training, down-weighting low-quality demonstrations. Empirically, Dexora outperforms competitive VLA baselines on both basic and dexterous benchmarks (e.g., average dexterous success 66.7% vs. 51.7%), attains 90% success on basic tasks, and shows robust out-of-distribution and cross-embodiment generalization. Ablations confirm the importance of real data and the discriminator for dexterity.

ReThinkLab.title: WorldArena 2.0: Extending Embodied World Model Benchmarking on Modality, Functionality and Platform
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yu Shang, Yinzhou Tang, Yiding Ma, Zhuohang Li, Lei Jin
ReThinkLab.summary: WorldArena 2.0 is a comprehensive benchmark that enhances embodied world model evaluation by incorporating multimodal perception, interactive functionality, and diverse real-world platforms.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: World models have emerged as a central paradigm for embodied intelligence, enabling agents to predict action-conditioned future and reason about environmental dynamics. However, existing embodied world model benchmarks are still largely confined to vision-only prediction, offline embodied applications, and simulator-based evaluation, making them insufficient for assessing increasingly comprehensive world models. In this work, we introduce WorldArena 2.0, an expanded benchmark that systematically broadens embodied world model evaluation along three dimensions: modality, functionality, and platform. Along the modality dimension, WorldArena 2.0 extends evaluation from vision-only to visuotactile modalities, enabling assessment of multimodal perception and prediction. Along the functionality dimension, it extends beyond policy evaluation and planning to assess world models as interactive RL environments for policy optimization. Along the platform dimension, it moves beyond simulator-only evaluation to a diverse suite of simulated and real-world robotic settings across multiple embodiments. Under a standardized protocol, WorldArena 2.0 comprehensively evaluates perceptual quality, interactive utility, and cross-platform performance, providing a comprehensive testbed for tracking progress toward embodied world models. The benchmark is available at: this https URL.

ReThinkLab.title: VoxScene: Anchor-Conditioned Voxel Diffusion for Indoor Scene Arrangement
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Haotian Mao, Yuhan Huang, Jiatao Lin, Yang Zhao, Hui Wang
ReThinkLab.summary: VoxScene introduces an anchor-conditioned voxel diffusion framework for 3D scene synthesis, ensuring collision-free arrangements and high-fidelity voxel outputs in complex environments.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: We present VoxScene, a novel anchor-conditioned voxel diffusion framework tailored for 3D scene synthesis. Current data-driven layout generation techniques typically rely on bounding proxies or implicit representations, which overlook volumetric structures. This geometric blindness inevitably leads to severe physical collisions and structural entanglement, particularly in densely populated environments. To overcome these limitations, we shift the paradigm to an explicit, object-centric voxel representation. Our pipeline sequentially synthesizes discrete volumetric occupancies conditioned on prior anchors and local context. By exploiting the mutually exclusive nature of discrete voxels, our approach eliminates spatial ambiguities and guarantees collision-free arrangements, even in highly complex environments. Furthermore, the synthesized high-fidelity voxel grids serve as discriminative geometric queries for downstream asset retrieval. Extensive experiments demonstrate the universality of our method, achieving state-of-the-art physical plausibility and unlocking shape diversity compared to existing layout planners.

ReThinkLab.title: Resolving Representation Ambiguity in Feedforward Novel View Synthesis Transformer via Semantic-Spatial Decoupling
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yihang Wu, Yihang Sun, Shaofeng Zhang, Zuxuan Wu, Junchi Yan
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper presents a novel approach for feedforward novel view synthesis transformers that decouples semantic and spatial representations to enhance rendering fidelity without increasing inference latency.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Transformer-based models have advanced feedforward novel view synthesis (NVS). Current architectures such as GS-LRM and LVSM mix semantic information (e.g., RGB) and spatial information (e.g., Plücker rays) into a shared feature space. Since Plücker rays naturally carry lattice-like spatial structure, these designs can make the spatial bias interfere with appearance representation and degrade rendering fidelity. To this end, we propose to decouple the representation of feedforward NVS transformers into separate semantic and spatial tokens. The decoupled design keeps semantic and spatial information explicit in their branches while preserving cross-branch interaction through shared attention routing. Built on this design, we introduce optional categorized supervision and bidirectional modulation: the former provides branch-specific training signals, while the latter improves interaction between the two branches. Notably, the base decoupled design introduces virtually zero additional inference latency due to its architectural design. The proposed designs achieve consistent improvements, demonstrating effectiveness across decoder-only and encoder-decoder feedforward NVS models.

ReThinkLab.title: Bench2Drive-Robust: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving under Deployment Perturbations
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhenghao Jin, Yanlun Peng, Xianda Guo, Haoran Liu
ReThinkLab.summary: Bench2Drive-Robust introduces a device-centric benchmark for evaluating closed-loop autonomous driving robustness against realistic deployment perturbations, highlighting significant challenges often overlooked by traditional methods.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Robustness is a critical requirement for deploying autonomous driving systems in the real world. Existing robustness benchmarks for autonomous driving have made important progress in studying the effects of image-level corruptions, such as adverse weather or camera degradation, on perception modules and open-loop planning outputs. However, deployment can also involve system-level imperfections, such as inference latency and ego-state estimation errors, which remain less studied in closed-loop E2E-AD evaluation. These imperfections can accumulate through the feedback loop and destabilize control. In this work, we present Bench2Drive-Robust, to our knowledge the first device-centric robustness benchmark for closed-loop end-to-end autonomous driving under realistic deployment perturbations. We systematically evaluate deployment-oriented perturbations arising from three major sources: camera-stream failures (frame drop, partial observation), ego-state estimation errors (GPS noise, and speed or odometry errors), and compute-induced control delay (model inference delay). We evaluate representative end-to-end driving methods and analyze their robustness under different perturbation severities. Our results show that these deployment-related perturbations can substantially degrade closed-loop driving performance, revealing robustness challenges that are not fully captured by conventional image-level corruption evaluations. By establishing a closed-loop evaluation protocol and demonstrating the substantial impact of these deployment-oriented perturbations, Bench2Drive-Robust defines practical robustness problems for end-to-end autonomous driving and encourages further research on deployment-aware robust driving systems.

ReThinkLab.title: An Efficient Streaming Video Understanding Framework with Agentic Control
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Jinming Liu, Jianguo Huang, Zhaoyang Jia, Jiahao Li, Xiaoyi Zhang
ReThinkLab.summary: The R3-Streaming framework enhances dynamic video understanding by using an adaptive cascaded control approach for efficient memory management and compute routing, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Streaming video requires handling dynamic information density under strict latency budgets. Yet, existing methods typically employ static strategies, such as fixed memory compression or reliance on a single model, forcing a trade-off: fast models fail on complex queries, while always-on heavy models violate real-time constraints and overcomplicate simple queries. Rather than fixing these decisions upfront, we propose R3-Streaming (Remember, Respond, Reason), which formulates streaming video understanding as a cascaded control problem: for each query, the system compresses memory, judges response readiness, and routes computation sequentially, so that each downstream decision builds on progressively refined information states. To optimize this pipeline, we introduce an age-aware forgetting policy for memory compression, as aggressively compressing historical frames can yield substantial performance gains. For compute routing, we propose TB-GRPO, a target-balanced reinforcement learning objective that routes hard queries to a stronger model while preventing mode collapse. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that R3-Streaming achieves state-of-the-art results among streaming MLLMs, reaching 57.92 on OVO-Bench and 76.36 on StreamingBench, while reducing visual token usage by 95 to 96 percent.

ReThinkLab.title: Entropy-Gradient Inversion: Moving Toward Internal Mechanism of Large Reasoning Models
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Junyao Yang, Chen Qian, Kun Wang, Linfeng Zhang, Quanshi Zhang
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper introduces Entropy-Gradient Inversion and Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO) to enhance reasoning capabilities in Large Reasoning Models through improved reinforcement learning techniques.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: The advancement of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift from reactive ``fast thinking'' text generation to systematic, step-by-step ``slow thinking'' reasoning, unlocking state-of-the-art performance in complex mathematical and logical tasks. However, the field faces \textit{the fundamental gap between token-level behavioral analysis and internal reasoning mechanisms, and the instability of reinforcement learning (RL) for reasoning optimization relying on costly external verifiers}. We identify and formally define \textbf{Entropy-Gradient Inversion}, a robust negative correlation between token entropy and logit gradients that acts as a definitive geometric fingerprint for LRM reasoning capability. Building on this, we propose \textbf{Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO)}, which embeds this inversion signature into RL reward regularization. Extensive experiments on various reasoning benchmarks across multiple model scales show CorR-PO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, confirming that stronger inversion directly correlates with superior reasoning performance.

ReThinkLab.title: Dynamic Execution Commitment of Vision-Language-Action Models
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Feng Chen, Xianghui Wang, Yuxuan Chen, Boying Li, Yefei He
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper introduces A3, an Adaptive Action Acceptance mechanism that optimizes dynamic execution commitment in Vision-Language-Action models by improving reliability and efficiency without manual horizon tuning.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models predominantly adopt action chunking, i.e., predicting and committing to a short horizon of consecutive low-level actions in a single forward pass, to amortize the inference cost of large-scale backbones and reduce per-step latency. However, committing these multi-step predictions to real-world execution requires balancing success rate against inference efficiency, a decision typically governed by fixed execution horizons tuned per task. Such heuristics ignore the state-dependent nature of predictive reliability, leading to brittle performance in dynamic or out-of-distribution settings. In this paper, we introduce A3, an Adaptive Action Acceptance mechanism that reframes dynamic execution commitment as a self-speculative prefix verification problem. A3 first computes a trajectory-wise consensus score of actions via group sampling, then selects a representative draft and prioritizes downstream verification. Specifically, it enforces: (1) consensus-ordered conditional invariance, which validates low-consensus actions by judging whether they remain consistent when re-decoded conditioned on high-consensus actions; and (2) prefix-closed sequential consistency, which guarantees physical rollout integrity by accepting only the longest continuous sequence of verified actions starting from the beginning. Consequently, the execution horizon emerges as the longest verifiable prefix satisfying both internal model logic and sequential execution constraints. Experiments across diverse VLA models and benchmarks demonstrate that A3 eliminates the need for manual horizon tuning while achieving a superior trade-off between execution robustness and inference throughput.

ReThinkLab.title: UST-Hand: An Uncertainty-aware Spatiotemporal Point Cloud Interaction Network for 3D Self-supervised Hand Pose Estimation
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Tianhao Han, Haoyang Zhang, Liang Xie, Haochen Chang, Kun Gao
ReThinkLab.summary: UST-Hand introduces a robust self-supervised 3D hand pose estimation framework that leverages uncertainty modeling and probabilistic point clouds to enhance accuracy and stability against noise.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Manually annotating accurate 3D hand poses is extremely time-consuming and labor-intensive. Existing self-supervised hand pose estimation methods leverage the discrepancy between input images and rendered outputs, or multi-view consistency constraints, as the driving force to optimize networks and progressively refine pose accuracy. However, these methods are highly susceptible to noisy pseudo-labels and overlook the importance of fully exploiting fine-grained spatial correlations, which undermines the stability of model training. To address these issues, we propose UST-Hand, a self-supervised learning framework that estimates uncertainty distribution of hand pose and constructs a probabilistic point cloud feature space, which enables the complex spatiotemporal relationship modeling. UST-Hand employs a conditional normalizing flow model to capture hand pose distributions and samples diverse hypotheses, facilitating robust learning under noisy pseudo-labels supervision with enhanced stability. These multi-hypothesis are mapped to a unified probabilistic 3D point cloud space for multi-view and temporal feature interaction, comprehensively exploring hand motion patterns and fine-grained spatial correlations. Extensive experiments on three challenging datasets demonstrate that UST-Hand achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing self-supervised methods by up to 37.8% in Mean Per Vertex Position Error (MPVPE).

ReThinkLab.title: Rethinking Point Clouds as Sequences: A Causal Next-Token Predictive Learning Framework
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yumeng Yao, Jingzhi Dong, Haowen Gu, Tao Chen, Zonghan Wu
ReThinkLab.summary: This paper introduces PointNTP, a novel approach for point cloud pre-training that utilizes a causal transformer for next-token prediction, enhancing self-supervised learning without reconstruction decoders.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: With the rapid progress of multimodal foundation models and predictive pre-training, an important open question is how to equip 3D point clouds with a pre-training paradigm that is better aligned with next-token and next-embedding learning. Existing point-cloud self-supervised methods are largely built on masked reconstruction or explicit geometric generation, and thus remain tied to input recovery rather than predictive dependency modeling. In this paper, we introduce PointNTP, which reformulates point cloud pre-training as a fully causal, decoder-free latent Next-Token Prediction problem. Specifically, each point cloud is first partitioned into local patches and serialized into a structured 3D token sequence according to patch-center geometry. The resulting sequence is then modeled by a causal Transformer under prefix-only conditioning, and trained with a shift-based prediction objective stabilized by stop-gradient targets. This design enables the model to learn structural dependencies directly in latent space, without reconstruction decoders or explicit geometric recovery. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed PointNTP is highly competitive across multiple downstream tasks: it achieves 93.8%(+0.5%), 92.6%(+0.3%), and 89.3%(+1.1%) on OBJ_BG, OBJ_ONLY, and PB_T50_RS of ScanObjectNN, respectively; obtains 85.0%(+0.1%) in this http URL on ShapeNetPart; and reaches 71.1% mAcc on S3DIS Area 5. Overall, decoder-free causal latent prediction provides a simple, scalable, and potentially modality-agnostic paradigm for point-cloud self-supervised learning, offering a new 3D perspective on foundation-style predictive learning for 3D data.

ReThinkLab.title: Mamba-VGGT: Persistent Long-Sequence Video Geometry Grounded Transformer via External Sliding Window Mamba Memory
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Tianchen Deng, Zhenxiang Xiong, Nailin Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Jiuming Liu
ReThinkLab.summary: Mamba-VGGT introduces a Sliding Window Mamba memory module enhancing long-sequence video geometry grounding, mitigating geometric drift while maintaining spatial consistency and reducing errors.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers (VGGT) have set new benchmarks in high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction. However, as the sequence length increases, these models suffer from catastrophic geometric forgetting and accumulation drift, primarily due to the quadratic complexity of global attention which necessitates truncated temporal windows. To overcome the resulting geometric drift, we present Mamba-VGGT, an enhanced VGGT framework capable of persistent long-range reasoning. Our key contribution is a Sliding Window Mamba (SWM) memory module that maintains an explicit external memory token across temporal windows. This module leverages selective state-space modeling to distill and propagate global geometric priors, effectively bypassing the memory constraints of traditional transformers. To integrate these long-term temporal cues without disrupting the highly optimized spatial features of the pre-trained VGGT, we propose a Zero-Init Spatial Memory Injector. Utilizing zero-convolutional layers, this injector adaptively fuses persistent memory into the patch token stream, ensuring structural stability and seamless feature alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing VGGT-based methods in maintaining spatial consistency and reducing trajectory accumulation errors. Our work provides a scalable, linear-complexity solution for geometry-grounded world modeling in extensive 3D environments.

ReThinkLab.title: Attention Hijacking: Response Manipulation Across Queries in Vision-Language Models
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zhiqiang Wang, Dongrui Liu, Yan Li, Zonghao Ying, Wei Xue
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper introduces "Attention Hijacking," an adversarial attack that enhances cross-query response manipulation in vision-language models by stabilizing image-dominant attention patterns.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Existing adversarial attacks on vision-language models (VLMs) can steer model outputs toward attacker-specified target responses, but their effectiveness often degrades when the same perturbed input is paired with different textual queries. This paper studies cross-query response manipulation, where a single adversarial example is expected to remain effective across diverse user queries. We first analyze the limitations of existing attacks and find that successful transfer is closely associated with preserving an image-dominant attention pattern during response generation. Motivated by the observation, we propose \textbf{Attention Hijacking}, a novel adversarial attack that explicitly steers internal attention distributions toward a persistent image-dominant pattern. By amplifying the influence of visual tokens on target response tokens while suppressing the competing influence of textual tokens, our method reduces the dependence of the manipulated output on the specific wording of the query. Extensive experiments on widely used VLMs show that Attention Hijacking substantially improves cross-query transferability across diverse target responses and unseen queries. The method also extends effectively to multiple attack scenarios, offering new insights into the role of attention stability in transferable response manipulation for VLMs.

ReThinkLab.title: Skills on the Fly: Test-Time Adaptive Skill Synthesis for LLM Agents
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Jingxing Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Zhihui Fu, Jun Wang, Weiwen Liu
ReThinkLab.summary: The SkillTTA method enhances LLM agents' adaptability by synthesizing task-specific skills from relevant training trajectories, improving performance on various benchmarks without updating the solver model.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: LLM agents benefit from reusable skills, yet test-time tasks often require guidance more specific than a static skill library can provide. We propose \emph{SkillTTA}, a Test-Time Adaptive Skill Synthesis method that retrieves a small set of training trajectories relevant to the current task and synthesizes them into a temporary, task-specific textual skill. The solver model is kept fixed, so adaptation happens entirely through generated context rather than parameter updates. We evaluate the method on SpreadsheetBench, ALFWorld, and BigCodeBench. Compared with static trajectory-to-skill synthesis using GPT-5.5, task-specific skills improve SpreadsheetBench Pass@1 from 0.397 to 0.505 and BigCodeBench Pass@1 from 0.517 to 0.651. On ALFWorld, the method matches a heavier memory-learning baseline within four points of success rate while producing the shortest successful trajectories among reported methods. Ablations on SpreadsheetBench further show that synthesized skills outperform raw trajectory prompting, that top-$k$ retrieval should stay small, and that failed trajectories are especially useful because they expose recurring evaluator-facing mistakes.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yihang Wu, Yihang Sun, Shaofeng Zhang, Zuxuan Wu, Junchi Yan
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper presents a novel approach for feedforward novel view synthesis transformers that decouples semantic and spatial representations to enhance rendering fidelity without increasing inference latency.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Transformer-based models have advanced feedforward novel view synthesis (NVS). Current architectures such as GS-LRM and LVSM mix semantic information (e.g., RGB) and spatial information (e.g., Plücker rays) into a shared feature space. Since Plücker rays naturally carry lattice-like spatial structure, these designs can make the spatial bias interfere with appearance representation and degrade rendering fidelity. To this end, we propose to decouple the representation of feedforward NVS transformers into separate semantic and spatial tokens. The decoupled design keeps semantic and spatial information explicit in their branches while preserving cross-branch interaction through shared attention routing. Built on this design, we introduce optional categorized supervision and bidirectional modulation: the former provides branch-specific training signals, while the latter improves interaction between the two branches. Notably, the base decoupled design introduces virtually zero additional inference latency due to its architectural design. The proposed designs achieve consistent improvements, demonstrating effectiveness across decoder-only and encoder-decoder feedforward NVS models.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Bench2Drive-Robust: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving under Deployment Perturbations
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhenghao Jin, Yanlun Peng, Xianda Guo, Haoran Liu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: Bench2Drive-Robust introduces a device-centric benchmark for evaluating closed-loop autonomous driving robustness against realistic deployment perturbations, highlighting significant challenges often overlooked by traditional methods.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Robustness is a critical requirement for deploying autonomous driving systems in the real world. Existing robustness benchmarks for autonomous driving have made important progress in studying the effects of image-level corruptions, such as adverse weather or camera degradation, on perception modules and open-loop planning outputs. However, deployment can also involve system-level imperfections, such as inference latency and ego-state estimation errors, which remain less studied in closed-loop E2E-AD evaluation. These imperfections can accumulate through the feedback loop and destabilize control. In this work, we present Bench2Drive-Robust, to our knowledge the first device-centric robustness benchmark for closed-loop end-to-end autonomous driving under realistic deployment perturbations. We systematically evaluate deployment-oriented perturbations arising from three major sources: camera-stream failures (frame drop, partial observation), ego-state estimation errors (GPS noise, and speed or odometry errors), and compute-induced control delay (model inference delay). We evaluate representative end-to-end driving methods and analyze their robustness under different perturbation severities. Our results show that these deployment-related perturbations can substantially degrade closed-loop driving performance, revealing robustness challenges that are not fully captured by conventional image-level corruption evaluations. By establishing a closed-loop evaluation protocol and demonstrating the substantial impact of these deployment-oriented perturbations, Bench2Drive-Robust defines practical robustness problems for end-to-end autonomous driving and encourages further research on deployment-aware robust driving systems.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: An Efficient Streaming Video Understanding Framework with Agentic Control
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Jinming Liu, Jianguo Huang, Zhaoyang Jia, Jiahao Li, Xiaoyi Zhang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The R3-Streaming framework enhances dynamic video understanding by using an adaptive cascaded control approach for efficient memory management and compute routing, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Streaming video requires handling dynamic information density under strict latency budgets. Yet, existing methods typically employ static strategies, such as fixed memory compression or reliance on a single model, forcing a trade-off: fast models fail on complex queries, while always-on heavy models violate real-time constraints and overcomplicate simple queries. Rather than fixing these decisions upfront, we propose R3-Streaming (Remember, Respond, Reason), which formulates streaming video understanding as a cascaded control problem: for each query, the system compresses memory, judges response readiness, and routes computation sequentially, so that each downstream decision builds on progressively refined information states. To optimize this pipeline, we introduce an age-aware forgetting policy for memory compression, as aggressively compressing historical frames can yield substantial performance gains. For compute routing, we propose TB-GRPO, a target-balanced reinforcement learning objective that routes hard queries to a stronger model while preventing mode collapse. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that R3-Streaming achieves state-of-the-art results among streaming MLLMs, reaching 57.92 on OVO-Bench and 76.36 on StreamingBench, while reducing visual token usage by 95 to 96 percent.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Entropy-Gradient Inversion: Moving Toward Internal Mechanism of Large Reasoning Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Junyao Yang, Chen Qian, Kun Wang, Linfeng Zhang, Quanshi Zhang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper introduces Entropy-Gradient Inversion and Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO) to enhance reasoning capabilities in Large Reasoning Models through improved reinforcement learning techniques.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: The advancement of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) has catalyzed a paradigm shift from reactive ``fast thinking'' text generation to systematic, step-by-step ``slow thinking'' reasoning, unlocking state-of-the-art performance in complex mathematical and logical tasks. However, the field faces \textit{the fundamental gap between token-level behavioral analysis and internal reasoning mechanisms, and the instability of reinforcement learning (RL) for reasoning optimization relying on costly external verifiers}. We identify and formally define \textbf{Entropy-Gradient Inversion}, a robust negative correlation between token entropy and logit gradients that acts as a definitive geometric fingerprint for LRM reasoning capability. Building on this, we propose \textbf{Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO)}, which embeds this inversion signature into RL reward regularization. Extensive experiments on various reasoning benchmarks across multiple model scales show CorR-PO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, confirming that stronger inversion directly correlates with superior reasoning performance.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Dynamic Execution Commitment of Vision-Language-Action Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Feng Chen, Xianghui Wang, Yuxuan Chen, Boying Li, Yefei He
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper introduces A3, an Adaptive Action Acceptance mechanism that optimizes dynamic execution commitment in Vision-Language-Action models by improving reliability and efficiency without manual horizon tuning.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models predominantly adopt action chunking, i.e., predicting and committing to a short horizon of consecutive low-level actions in a single forward pass, to amortize the inference cost of large-scale backbones and reduce per-step latency. However, committing these multi-step predictions to real-world execution requires balancing success rate against inference efficiency, a decision typically governed by fixed execution horizons tuned per task. Such heuristics ignore the state-dependent nature of predictive reliability, leading to brittle performance in dynamic or out-of-distribution settings. In this paper, we introduce A3, an Adaptive Action Acceptance mechanism that reframes dynamic execution commitment as a self-speculative prefix verification problem. A3 first computes a trajectory-wise consensus score of actions via group sampling, then selects a representative draft and prioritizes downstream verification. Specifically, it enforces: (1) consensus-ordered conditional invariance, which validates low-consensus actions by judging whether they remain consistent when re-decoded conditioned on high-consensus actions; and (2) prefix-closed sequential consistency, which guarantees physical rollout integrity by accepting only the longest continuous sequence of verified actions starting from the beginning. Consequently, the execution horizon emerges as the longest verifiable prefix satisfying both internal model logic and sequential execution constraints. Experiments across diverse VLA models and benchmarks demonstrate that A3 eliminates the need for manual horizon tuning while achieving a superior trade-off between execution robustness and inference throughput.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: UST-Hand: An Uncertainty-aware Spatiotemporal Point Cloud Interaction Network for 3D Self-supervised Hand Pose Estimation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Tianhao Han, Haoyang Zhang, Liang Xie, Haochen Chang, Kun Gao
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: UST-Hand introduces a robust self-supervised 3D hand pose estimation framework that leverages uncertainty modeling and probabilistic point clouds to enhance accuracy and stability against noise.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Manually annotating accurate 3D hand poses is extremely time-consuming and labor-intensive. Existing self-supervised hand pose estimation methods leverage the discrepancy between input images and rendered outputs, or multi-view consistency constraints, as the driving force to optimize networks and progressively refine pose accuracy. However, these methods are highly susceptible to noisy pseudo-labels and overlook the importance of fully exploiting fine-grained spatial correlations, which undermines the stability of model training. To address these issues, we propose UST-Hand, a self-supervised learning framework that estimates uncertainty distribution of hand pose and constructs a probabilistic point cloud feature space, which enables the complex spatiotemporal relationship modeling. UST-Hand employs a conditional normalizing flow model to capture hand pose distributions and samples diverse hypotheses, facilitating robust learning under noisy pseudo-labels supervision with enhanced stability. These multi-hypothesis are mapped to a unified probabilistic 3D point cloud space for multi-view and temporal feature interaction, comprehensively exploring hand motion patterns and fine-grained spatial correlations. Extensive experiments on three challenging datasets demonstrate that UST-Hand achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing self-supervised methods by up to 37.8% in Mean Per Vertex Position Error (MPVPE).

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Rethinking Point Clouds as Sequences: A Causal Next-Token Predictive Learning Framework
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yumeng Yao, Jingzhi Dong, Haowen Gu, Tao Chen, Zonghan Wu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: This paper introduces PointNTP, a novel approach for point cloud pre-training that utilizes a causal transformer for next-token prediction, enhancing self-supervised learning without reconstruction decoders.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: With the rapid progress of multimodal foundation models and predictive pre-training, an important open question is how to equip 3D point clouds with a pre-training paradigm that is better aligned with next-token and next-embedding learning. Existing point-cloud self-supervised methods are largely built on masked reconstruction or explicit geometric generation, and thus remain tied to input recovery rather than predictive dependency modeling. In this paper, we introduce PointNTP, which reformulates point cloud pre-training as a fully causal, decoder-free latent Next-Token Prediction problem. Specifically, each point cloud is first partitioned into local patches and serialized into a structured 3D token sequence according to patch-center geometry. The resulting sequence is then modeled by a causal Transformer under prefix-only conditioning, and trained with a shift-based prediction objective stabilized by stop-gradient targets. This design enables the model to learn structural dependencies directly in latent space, without reconstruction decoders or explicit geometric recovery. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed PointNTP is highly competitive across multiple downstream tasks: it achieves 93.8%(+0.5%), 92.6%(+0.3%), and 89.3%(+1.1%) on OBJ_BG, OBJ_ONLY, and PB_T50_RS of ScanObjectNN, respectively; obtains 85.0%(+0.1%) in this http URL on ShapeNetPart; and reaches 71.1% mAcc on S3DIS Area 5. Overall, decoder-free causal latent prediction provides a simple, scalable, and potentially modality-agnostic paradigm for point-cloud self-supervised learning, offering a new 3D perspective on foundation-style predictive learning for 3D data.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Mamba-VGGT: Persistent Long-Sequence Video Geometry Grounded Transformer via External Sliding Window Mamba Memory
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Tianchen Deng, Zhenxiang Xiong, Nailin Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Jiuming Liu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: Mamba-VGGT introduces a Sliding Window Mamba memory module enhancing long-sequence video geometry grounding, mitigating geometric drift while maintaining spatial consistency and reducing errors.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers (VGGT) have set new benchmarks in high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction. However, as the sequence length increases, these models suffer from catastrophic geometric forgetting and accumulation drift, primarily due to the quadratic complexity of global attention which necessitates truncated temporal windows. To overcome the resulting geometric drift, we present Mamba-VGGT, an enhanced VGGT framework capable of persistent long-range reasoning. Our key contribution is a Sliding Window Mamba (SWM) memory module that maintains an explicit external memory token across temporal windows. This module leverages selective state-space modeling to distill and propagate global geometric priors, effectively bypassing the memory constraints of traditional transformers. To integrate these long-term temporal cues without disrupting the highly optimized spatial features of the pre-trained VGGT, we propose a Zero-Init Spatial Memory Injector. Utilizing zero-convolutional layers, this injector adaptively fuses persistent memory into the patch token stream, ensuring structural stability and seamless feature alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing VGGT-based methods in maintaining spatial consistency and reducing trajectory accumulation errors. Our work provides a scalable, linear-complexity solution for geometry-grounded world modeling in extensive 3D environments.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Attention Hijacking: Response Manipulation Across Queries in Vision-Language Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Zhiqiang Wang, Dongrui Liu, Yan Li, Zonghao Ying, Wei Xue
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper introduces "Attention Hijacking," an adversarial attack that enhances cross-query response manipulation in vision-language models by stabilizing image-dominant attention patterns.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Existing adversarial attacks on vision-language models (VLMs) can steer model outputs toward attacker-specified target responses, but their effectiveness often degrades when the same perturbed input is paired with different textual queries. This paper studies cross-query response manipulation, where a single adversarial example is expected to remain effective across diverse user queries. We first analyze the limitations of existing attacks and find that successful transfer is closely associated with preserving an image-dominant attention pattern during response generation. Motivated by the observation, we propose \textbf{Attention Hijacking}, a novel adversarial attack that explicitly steers internal attention distributions toward a persistent image-dominant pattern. By amplifying the influence of visual tokens on target response tokens while suppressing the competing influence of textual tokens, our method reduces the dependence of the manipulated output on the specific wording of the query. Extensive experiments on widely used VLMs show that Attention Hijacking substantially improves cross-query transferability across diverse target responses and unseen queries. The method also extends effectively to multiple attack scenarios, offering new insights into the role of attention stability in transferable response manipulation for VLMs.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Skills on the Fly: Test-Time Adaptive Skill Synthesis for LLM Agents
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Jingxing Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Zhihui Fu, Jun Wang, Weiwen Liu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The SkillTTA method enhances LLM agents' adaptability by synthesizing task-specific skills from relevant training trajectories, improving performance on various benchmarks without updating the solver model.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: LLM agents benefit from reusable skills, yet test-time tasks often require guidance more specific than a static skill library can provide. We propose \emph{SkillTTA}, a Test-Time Adaptive Skill Synthesis method that retrieves a small set of training trajectories relevant to the current task and synthesizes them into a temporary, task-specific textual skill. The solver model is kept fixed, so adaptation happens entirely through generated context rather than parameter updates. We evaluate the method on SpreadsheetBench, ALFWorld, and BigCodeBench. Compared with static trajectory-to-skill synthesis using GPT-5.5, task-specific skills improve SpreadsheetBench Pass@1 from 0.397 to 0.505 and BigCodeBench Pass@1 from 0.517 to 0.651. On ALFWorld, the method matches a heavier memory-learning baseline within four points of success rate while producing the shortest successful trajectories among reported methods. Ablations on SpreadsheetBench further show that synthesized skills outperform raw trajectory prompting, that top-$k$ retrieval should stay small, and that failed trajectories are especially useful because they expose recurring evaluator-facing mistakes.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: VGGT-Occ: Geometry-Grounded and Density-Aware Gated Fusion for 3D Occupancy Prediction
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Xun Chen, Tianchen Deng, Rui Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Junyi Ma
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: VGGT-Occ introduces a geometry-infused framework with Projection-Aware Deformable Attention for enhanced 3D occupancy prediction, achieving superior performance with fewer parameters.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction requires accurate 2D-to-3D feature lifting, yet current methods restrict camera geometry to initial projections. Subsequent operations like offset learning, attention weighting, and cross-camera aggregation remain geometry-agnostic, ignoring essential physical constraints. We propose VGGT-Occ, a framework that embeds geometric tokens throughout the entire pipeline. We introduce Projection-Aware Deformable Attention (PA-DA) to inject geometry into all attention stages. PA-DA projects 3D offsets back to image planes and leverages the projection Jacobian as an additive bias to suppress unreliable observations. Features are then integrated through a view-quality semantic gate for cross-view consistency. To optimize both efficiency and performance, we employ a sequential coarse-to-fine decoder with gated fusion, where low-resolution features are refined into higher resolutions, allocating computation by information density while substantially reducing decoder cost. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our approach. On SurroundOcc-nuScenes, VGGT-Occ achieves 33.00\% IoU and 21.08\% mIoU ($T{=}1$), and 33.64\% IoU and 21.43\% mIoU with $T{=}2$ inference, outperforming existing methods, with only ${\sim}41$M trainable parameters in the occupancy head. Code will be released publicly.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: OrbiSim: World Models as Differentiable Physics Engines for Embodied Intelligence
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Jiajian Li, Jingyuan Huang, Junru Gong, Qi Wang, Xiaokang Yang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: OrbiSim is a differentiable physics engine that unifies structured scene assets and neural dynamics to enhance robotic simulation and reinforcement learning performance.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: We present OrbiSim, a novel robotic simulation paradigm that redefines world models as a fully differentiable physics engine for embodied intelligence. Unlike prior world models that focus on unconstrained imagination in latent or visual domains, OrbiSim establishes a unified, physically-grounded pathway that bridges structured scene assets, neural dynamics, and downstream reinforcement learning. By enabling end-to-end differentiability throughout the entire simulation loop -- spanning from explicit state transitions to visual observation generation -- OrbiSim supports tasks traditionally intractable for classical simulators, such as differentiable contact modeling, gradient-based policy optimization under sparse rewards, and intuitive physical inference. Empirical results demonstrate that OrbiSim significantly outperforms state-of-the-art world models in both predictive fidelity and control performance. Furthermore, its consistent responsiveness to asset configurations and physical parameters suggests its potential as a differentiable tool for enhancing robot simulation and policy training.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Dexora: Open-source VLA for High-DoF Bimanual Dexterity
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Zongzheng Zhang, Jingrui Pang, Zhuo Yang, Kun Li, Minwen Liao
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: Dexora is an open-source Vision-Language-Action model enabling high-dimensional dexterous manipulation with dual-arm systems, surpassing existing benchmarks through innovative training methods and data quality management.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently become a central direction in embodied AI, but current systems are restricted to either dual-gripper control or single-arm dexterous hand manipulation. While low-dimensional gripper control can often be handled with simpler methods, high-dimensional dexterous hand control benefits greatly from full end-to-end VLA learning. In this work, we introduce Dexora, the first open-source VLA system that natively targets dual-arm, dual-hand high-DoF manipulation. We design a hybrid teleoperation pipeline that decouples gross arm kinematics (captured with a custom exoskeleton backpack) from fine finger motion (markerless hand tracking via Apple Vision Pro), and that drives both a physical dual-arm dual-hand platform and an identical MuJoCo digital twin. Using that interface, we assemble a large training corpus: an embodiment-matched synthetic corpus (100K simulated trajectories, 6.5M frames) and a real-world dataset of 10K teleoperated episodes (2.92M frames). To mitigate noisy teleoperation demonstrations, we propose a data-quality-aware training recipe: an offline discriminator provides clip-level weights for diffusion-transformer policy training, down-weighting low-quality demonstrations. Empirically, Dexora outperforms competitive VLA baselines on both basic and dexterous benchmarks (e.g., average dexterous success 66.7% vs. 51.7%), attains 90% success on basic tasks, and shows robust out-of-distribution and cross-embodiment generalization. Ablations confirm the importance of real data and the discriminator for dexterity.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: WorldArena 2.0: Extending Embodied World Model Benchmarking on Modality, Functionality and Platform
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Yu Shang, Yinzhou Tang, Yiding Ma, Zhuohang Li, Lei Jin
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: WorldArena 2.0 is a comprehensive benchmark that enhances embodied world model evaluation by incorporating multimodal perception, interactive functionality, and diverse real-world platforms.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: World models have emerged as a central paradigm for embodied intelligence, enabling agents to predict action-conditioned future and reason about environmental dynamics. However, existing embodied world model benchmarks are still largely confined to vision-only prediction, offline embodied applications, and simulator-based evaluation, making them insufficient for assessing increasingly comprehensive world models. In this work, we introduce WorldArena 2.0, an expanded benchmark that systematically broadens embodied world model evaluation along three dimensions: modality, functionality, and platform. Along the modality dimension, WorldArena 2.0 extends evaluation from vision-only to visuotactile modalities, enabling assessment of multimodal perception and prediction. Along the functionality dimension, it extends beyond policy evaluation and planning to assess world models as interactive RL environments for policy optimization. Along the platform dimension, it moves beyond simulator-only evaluation to a diverse suite of simulated and real-world robotic settings across multiple embodiments. Under a standardized protocol, WorldArena 2.0 comprehensively evaluates perceptual quality, interactive utility, and cross-platform performance, providing a comprehensive testbed for tracking progress toward embodied world models. The benchmark is available at: this https URL.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: VoxScene: Anchor-Conditioned Voxel Diffusion for Indoor Scene Arrangement
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Haotian Mao, Yuhan Huang, Jiatao Lin, Yang Zhao, Hui Wang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: VoxScene introduces an anchor-conditioned voxel diffusion framework for 3D scene synthesis, ensuring collision-free arrangements and high-fidelity voxel outputs in complex environments.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: We present VoxScene, a novel anchor-conditioned voxel diffusion framework tailored for 3D scene synthesis.
